title: Caesar: Optimizing Federated Learning via Low-deviation Compression

problem.claim: Compression is used to reduce federated learning communication overhead, but information loss can cause model or gradient deviation and degrade training performance under data heterogeneity and model obsolescence.

gap.claim: Existing compression approaches do not adequately control model or gradient deviation while reducing communication traffic.

contributions.claim: Caesar is an FL framework using low-deviation compression to balance model accuracy and traffic cost.
For global model download, Caesar greedily selects each device's compression ratio based on local-model staleness.
For local gradient upload, Caesar estimates gradient importance from local sample volume and label distribution to guide compression ratios.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe Caesar as a novel FL framework with a low-deviation compression approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors implemented Caesar on two physical platforms containing 40 smartphones and 80 NVIDIA Jetson devices.
The authors report that Caesar reduces traffic costs by about 25.54% to 37.88% at the same target accuracy compared with compression-based baselines.
The authors report only 0.68% degradation in final test accuracy relative to full-precision communication.

narrative_sequence.summary: Communication overhead motivates compression in federated learning.
Compression-induced information loss can produce model or gradient deviation and reduce training performance.
Caesar introduces low-deviation compression to trade off model accuracy and traffic cost.
The framework adapts download compression using model staleness and upload compression using local data properties.
The authors report a physical-platform implementation and traffic and accuracy results against compression baselines and full-precision communication.

source_observation.claim: Compression ratios are adapted separately for global model downloads and local gradient uploads using staleness and local data properties.

interpretation.claim: Communication compression can benefit from direction-specific, context-aware allocation rather than a single fixed ratio.

application.claim: In distributed training systems, use available device state and data characteristics to allocate compression where information loss is less harmful.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported federated learning setting and platforms.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, model architectures, or exact compression algorithms.
The abstract does not identify the compression-based baselines or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not report variance, statistical testing, or detailed communication and accuracy measurements.
